extracted.intended_audience: distance education practitioners, instructional designers, learning technologists, and higher-education faculty
extracted.subtask_description: Identify and apply functional criteria for designing or evaluating Educational Social Software (ESS) for distance and blended learning, with emphasis on supporting learner freedom, community, and cost-effective interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for learner freedoms
rubrics_metrics.description: ESS are defined as networked tools that support and encourage individuals to learn together while retaining individual control over their time, space, presence, activity, identity, and relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and evaluate ESS by whether they expand rather than constrain Paulsen’s dimensions of freedom (space, time, pace, media, access, content — plus freedom of relationship). Tools should allow choice and control across these dimensions; failure to permit such control reduces suitability for self-paced and continuous-enrolment learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow learners to make known (or conceal) their presence, both synchronously and asynchronously, including presence notification and indicators across text, audio and video tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence indicators should enable spontaneous interaction (e.g., instant messaging, chat meetups) but be under learner control so privacy/anonymity can be protected. Example/anti-pattern: systems that notify who is online (FirstClass) encourage chat; systems lacking presence notification (WebCT) see empty, unused chat rooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification (push and pull) and persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide both pushed and pulled forms of notification (RSS, instant messaging, email) when new content or communication is entered into a learning space, and allow historical and persistent display and searching of these interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality ESS should notify learners of new activity and also maintain searchable records so the learning space spans significant time. Evaluate whether notifications are timely, configurable, and whether the system preserves history for retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtering (spam control and relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contain collaborative filtering systems to filter out illegitimate information (spam) and filter in items of potential interest, supporting management of high volumes of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both filter-out effectiveness (spam mitigation) and filter-in effectiveness (recommending relevant items). Note limitations of current semantic web/RSS/FOAF tools; consider collaborative and reputation-based filters as part of the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperative learning support (cooperation vs collaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support cooperative activities — learner-encouraged but not compulsory interactions — which tend to be short-term, temporally bounded, and not tightly time-centric; distinguish these from compulsory collaborative activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design features that enable ad hoc, transient communities and allow learners to cooperate across varied schedules and contexts. Evaluate whether ESS supports both ephemeral cooperative activities and more tightly structured collaborative work, and whether it scales without imposing high instructor time costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral systems and activity-based referrals
rubrics_metrics.description: Track learner activities and indicators of success (time spent, assessments attempted and passed, formal evaluations) to produce referrals that guide learners to activities, courses, or peers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective ESS uses implicit referral/stigmergic models (activity trails like ant pheromones) to recommend resources and learning pathways. Evaluate how activity trails are captured, how referrals are surfaced, and how these are used to refine learning activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student modelling and learner profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify, classify, and quantify individual learner profiles (interests, learning styles, goals, accomplishments, progress, professional status, family status, etc.) to customize referrals, notifications, and filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles may be explicitly edited by learners or updated in real time by activity. Systems should expose profiles in machine-readable XML and support standards (IMS) so autonomous agents can use them. Crucially, learner profiles must be under the ultimate control of the learner to maintain trust and privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking resources with people (conjunction of personal and resource information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine personal information (who built, used, recommended, or commented on resources) with resource metadata to facilitate fine-grained searches and better matchmaking between learners and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether ESS enables searching/joining by both resource attributes and people-related signals (recommendations, commentary). Downes argues this conjunction facilitates much more fine-grained discovery than resource-only or person-only systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social discovery and introductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide selective referrals to other people, mining weak and strong ties so learners can be introduced to likely useful contacts and form productive learning relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mechanisms for social discovery (profiles, friend-lists, referrals), the ability to mine networks for probable useful connections, and support for reputation-building via documented postings and interactions to help evaluate others’ past contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for group functioning (decision making, memory, documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tools that help groups handle complexity and scale, including filtering, spam control, recommendation, social authentication, decision making, maintaining group memory, and documenting processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on Coates/Butterfield: evaluate whether ESS provides features that ease group tasks (voting, threaded archives, document versioning, audit trails) and whether these scale to larger distributed groups without overwhelming participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards, interoperability, and machine-readable exposure
rubrics_metrics.description: Expose learner profiles and related data in interoperable, XML-based formats and adhere to standards (such as IMS profiles) so data can be read/interpreted by humans and autonomous agents as part of an Educational Semantic Web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess conformity to relevant standards, availability of XML-based profile exports, and the ability to interoperate with external tools and agents. Ensure privacy controls accompany data exposure to maintain learner trust.
